rationale.hitl-workflow: Discrete human approval gates govern progression and arbitrate design trade-offs.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Compiler, linter, and test verdicts condition later phase progression.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Teach-backs and coverage matrices make AI activity inspectable to operators.
rationale.agent-scope-drift: Negative scope, inventories, and divergence checks bound implementation drift.
rationale.quality-debt: Framework targets technical debt, complexity inflation, coupling, and maintainability.
rationale.framework: Specifies a reusable eight-phase development and verification architecture.
rationale.built-system: Authors implemented the methodology as two Visual Studio Code extensions.
rationale.adopted: Multiple practitioners applied it across production R&D projects.
rationale.agentic: AI produces phased artifacts and modules reviewed at lifecycle gates.
rationale.steering: Problem discovery, specifications, and context shaping substantively guide generation.
rationale.metrics: Defines quality scores and thresholds for discovery, convergence, and approval.
rationale.risk-security: Universal security lens operationalizes attack-surface review before implementation.
rationale.risk-quality: Simplification, complexity audits, and testing mitigate non-security quality decay.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Teach-back and adversarial posture mitigate fluency-driven over-reliance.
rationale.method-field-study: Internal records summarize natural use across production R&D projects.
rationale.counterpoint: Opposes tool- and capability-centric accounts of AI development reliability.
